name: Electric-drive liquefaction (e-LNG)
applications: plants with cheap hydropower or grid power
principle: Large electric motors, rather than gas turbines, drive the refrigerant compressors in the liquefaction trains, so the plant burns no fuel gas for compression and, if power is low-carbon, has far lower CO2. Freeport LNG in Texas runs three electric-driven trains; Equinor's Hammerfest LNG plans to replace its gas turbine generators with power from shore.

process_steps.name: Electric power supply
equipment: grid connection or power from shore

reference_plants.name: Hammerfest LNG (Snohvit), Norway (Equinor) - all-electric liquefaction
reference_plants.capacity: world-scale LNG plant in which, for the first time, all main refrigeration compressors are electrically driven; Equinor investing about USD 1.3 bn to grid-connect and further electrify the plant

source.note: Offshore Energy (all main compressors electrically driven - a first for world-scale LNG); highnorthnews 22 Dec 2022 (USD 1.3 bn electrification investment); read 2026-10-28

reference_plants.name: Freeport LNG, Texas (electric-motor-driven refrigeration compressors)
reference_plants.capacity: three trains equipped with the largest electric motor-powered refrigeration compressors in the US; Train 1 commercial operation December 2019

source.note: NS Energy Business (largest electric-motor refrigeration compressors in the US); read 2026-10-28

advantages: No fuel-gas combustion at the compressors
Easier start and better availability than gas turbines (Freeport Train 2 test faster than Train 1, which is a learning effect, not proven)
limitations: CO2 benefit depends on the grid
